author: fab_10
content: I have a question about `testing_buildBlockV1` https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/api/methods/testing_buildBlockV1 and its behavior when there is a hard fork, for example what should happen when the EL passes form Osaka to Amsterdam?

author: boma_naps
content: From my understanding, the fork follows payloadAttributes.timestamp against client's fork schedule let say for example  Amsterdam timestamp on an Osaka parent will build a full Amsterdam block blockAccessList + slotNumber, and unlike the versioned getPayload/fcU there's no V2 or -38005 error, the method  tracks timestamp fork. one thing here to note is testing_buildBlockV1.yaml is still on the V3 shapes while we have engine/amsterdam.md already defines the fields, but I believe geth and the eels/build-block simulator already expect the Amsterdam output, so the yaml just needs a PR to catch up.

author: fab_10
content: ok so it should completely ignore the chain hard fork, and decide what to do based on the input timestamp

author: boma_naps
content: exactly, it still uses the chain's fork schedule, it just ignores what fork the parent was on and picks the rules from the input timestamp would also like <@372731338031366165>  and <@194432762315407360>  to weigh in on this since they authored the spec.

author: mysticryuujin
content: I authored the spec based on the Nethermind and Geth implementations 🫣 which was written for the testing teams, so it being underspecified is not unexpected 😅

author: mysticryuujin
content: I don't think we have a way to write a test fixture for a test AT a fork block either 🤔

author: boma_naps
content: ooh alright, maybe it would  be nice if the yaml stated the fork rule explicitly, fork follows attributes timestamp, Amsterdam shapes in the schemas am not sure if this makes sense? also one idea for the AT - fork case since the test chain is pre-generated past all its forks, we could add a future dated fork time e.g amsterdamTime past the chain end to the test genesis, then a fixture calling buildBlockV1 with a timestamp after activation would capture the transition block exactly the only real dependency is geth supporting amsterdamTime in the genesis config when the chain is regenerated.
